intro: Learn vocabulary for driving, traffic fines, breakdowns and road safety.
p.el cinturón.nota: In the sense of wearing a seat belt, use llevar puesto el cinturón or abrocharse el cinturón.
p.el seguro.nota: Insurance coverage depends on the policy.
p.la rueda.nota: In the phrase se pinchó una rueda, this refers to a tyre (UK) or tire (US).
p.la grúa.nota: A vehicle that tows a broken-down or illegally parked car.
p.conducir.nota: The first-person singular form is conduzco; the second-person singular is conduces.
b1.texto:
Useful driving verbs: **conducir**, **adelantar**, **frenar**, **girar** and **aparcar**. **Abrocharse el cinturón** means to fasten a seat belt; **llevar el carné de conducir** means to carry a driving licence.

Road features include **carriles**, **semáforos** and **pasos de cebra** for **peatones**. The general maximum speed for cars and motorcycles on Spanish motorways is 120 km/h; obey any lower speed shown on signs.

There may be **atascos**; drivers can get **multas** for speeding or parking badly; tyres can get punctures; cars can run out of petrol. From 2026, vehicles registered in Spain must use a connected **baliza V-16** to signal a vehicle immobilized by breakdown or accident. The beacon does not call the emergency services or a tow truck, so contact them separately.

Common road rules use impersonal forms: **no se puede adelantar** (overtaking is not allowed); **está prohibido aparcar** (parking is prohibited); **hay que ceder el paso a los peatones en los pasos de cebra** (drivers must give way to pedestrians); **es obligatorio abrocharse el cinturón** (seat belts must be fastened).
b2.f0: Sorry I'm late. There was a huge traffic jam on the motorway.
b2.f2: No. A lorry got a puncture and they closed a lane.
b2.f3: Well, yesterday I got a fine for parking on a zebra crossing.
b2.f5: The tow truck took it away. Thankfully, my insurance covers the repair.
b4.o1.refuerzo: Spanish puts a fine on you: poner una multa.
b4.o2.refuerzo: Spanish puts a fine on you: poner una multa.
b5.pregunta: Where do you take a car that has broken down?
b5.o2.refuerzo: That is the boot of the car.
b6.pregunta: Complete: wearing a seat belt is compulsory.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Use the infinitive after es obligatorio; this is the usual phrase for fastening a seat belt.
b6.o1.refuerzo: This is a conjugated verb, not an infinitive.
b6.o2.refuerzo: A gerund does not complete this construction.
b7.o1.explicacion: Se nos presents it as an accident that happened to us.
b8.pregunta: Who walks across a «paso de cebra»?
b9.traduccion: There was a huge traffic jam on the motorway.
b10.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Write about a journey by road: the route, the traffic and anything that happened.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Explain aloud to the police or to your insurance company how a small accident happened.
b11.pregunta: What is the connected V-16 beacon used for in Spain?
b11.o0.refuerzo: It warns other road users about a breakdown or accident.
b11.o1.refuerzo: You must contact roadside assistance separately.
b11.o2.refuerzo: Speed is measured by other devices.
